transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?
I’m just… exhausted. Worn out all the time. Even going from the bedroom to the kitchen feels like I’ve been hauling lumber all day. Resting doesn’t really seem to give me anything back.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, socializing, or activities you used to find pleasurable?

Yeah… I guess so. I used to do choir, play a little pickup ball, work on cars, grill when the family came around. Now I just… don’t care enough to go. Half the time I don’t even answer people’s texts.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah… most days. I wake up and it’s just this heavy feeling in my chest, like there’s no point. Some days I end up sitting out in the garage crying, and I don’t even really know why.
How long have you been feeling this way? Has this happened before, or is this the first time you've felt like this?
About four months, I think. It started after my wife went back to working full-time… I’ve been alone most weekdays since then. I don’t really know about before—not like this.
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, extremely energetic, or so confident that you didn’t sleep much but still felt fine?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had normal days here and there, but not like that—nothing where I didn’t need sleep and felt great or anything.
Have you ever had a period like this before where you felt so down and lost interest in things for two weeks or more?
I’m… not really sure. I don’t remember having it go on like this before, not for that long. This feels different, I guess.
Have you ever had a period like this before where you felt down and lost interest in things for several weeks or more, or is this definitely the first time you've felt this way for this long?
I don’t know if it’s definitely the first time… but this has been about four months now. Since my wife went back to full-time work and I’ve been alone most weekdays.
Before this current period, have you ever had any other times in your life where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that lasted for several weeks or longer?
I… I don’t really know. Maybe I had rough patches before, but I can’t say they lasted weeks like this. Nothing I can clearly point to.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that lasted for more than two weeks in a row?
I can’t really say. I’ve had bad spells, I guess, but I don’t remember anything before that was more than two weeks straight.
Before this current period, have you ever had any other episodes where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that lasted for more than two weeks at a time?
I don’t really remember any other time like that. I mean, I’ve had hard times, but not something I can say was more than two weeks like this.
Have you ever had at least one other episode before this current one where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that lasted for more than two weeks?
I don’t think so. I can’t really point to another time before this that was like that for more than two weeks.
Have you ever had at least two separate episodes in your life where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that each lasted for more than two weeks?
No… I don’t think I’ve had two separate times like that. I can’t really remember anything that fits.
Have you ever had at least two separate times in your life when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that each lasted for more than two weeks?
No, not that I can remember. I know you’ve asked, but… I don’t think there were two separate times like that.
Have you ever had two or more separate times in your life when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that each lasted for more than two weeks?
I don’t know… I really can’t say there were two separate times like that. I don’t remember it that way.

Can you think back over your life and say for sure whether there were at least two separate times when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that each lasted for more than two weeks?
I can’t say for sure. I’ve tried to think about it, but… I don’t really remember two separate times like that.

Looking back over your entire life, can you say for sure that there have been at least two separate times when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that each lasted for more than two weeks?
No… I can’t say that for sure. I don’t really have two separate times in mind like that.

Looking back over your entire life, can you say for sure that there have been at least two separate times when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had low energy that each lasted for more than two weeks?
I don’t think I can say that for sure. I just… don’t have it clear in my mind like that.

inference_history.note: The patient endorsed both fatigue and anhedonia, which are key symptoms of major depressive disorder, making other diagnoses like F48.0 (neurasthenia), F20.4 (schizophrenia, residual type), G72.81 (myopathy, unspecified), and R53.81 (other fatigue) less likely given the current presentation.

The duration of symptoms being approximately four months and the absence of a previous similar episode rule out F32.0 (Mild depressive episode) and F33.0 (Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode mild). The severity is at least moderate (F32.1/F33.1) given the functional impairment and persistent depressed mood. Severe (F32.2/F33.2) remains possible but not yet confirmed.

The patient denies having any prior episodes of depression lasting more than two weeks, which rules out recurrent depressive disorder (F33.1 and F33.2). This supports a diagnosis of a single episode of major depression, with severity codes F32.1 (moderate) or F32.2 (severe) still under consideration.

The patient has not reported any prior episodes of depressed mood, loss of interest, or low energy lasting more than two weeks, which makes the diagnosis of recurrent depressive disorder (F32.2) less likely. However, the current episode remains consistent with a moderate depressive episode (F32.1). No new information to rule out F32.1.

The patient has not provided clear evidence of a previous episode of depression lasting more than two weeks, nor confirmation of two separate episodes, leaving the distinction between mild and moderate severity uncertain. No new information was introduced to rule out either candidate definitively.

The patient has not been able to confirm with certainty whether there were at least two separate episodes of depression lasting more than two weeks prior to the current episode. This uncertainty maintains both F32.1 (moderate) and F32.2 (severe) as possible candidates, as the current episode is clearly major depressive in nature but the history of recurrence remains unclear.
